data.title: Chat: commit hashes and branch names in messages are click-to-copy

provenance.reason: board DM msg 793: explicit request for a Lattice task

data.to:
SOURCE: board DM msg 793 (human:forrest, 2026-09-11T18:15Z), verbatim: "I think we need to make commit hashes/branch names in chat messages clickable to copy. make an issue for this". Filed by cto-owen on behalf of the board (acked in msg 810).

WHAT "CLICKABLE TO COPY" MEANS, concretely:
  - A recognised commit hash (a bare 7-40 character lowercase hex run, word-bounded) or a branch name of the shape this company uses (feat/AS-<n>-<slug>; the planner decides whether to also admit other prefixes seen in history and should grep the chat export to find out what shapes actually occur) inside a message body renders as an inline element that, on plain click, writes the LITERAL matched text to the clipboard and shows a brief visual confirmation (e.g. a short-lived "copied" state on the element). No navigation, no href, no new tab. Modified clicks and ordinary text selection keep working as today.
  - Copy uses navigator.clipboard.writeText where available; the planner decides the fallback (execCommand copy on a selection, or simply no affordance) for insecure contexts. The tailnet page is https and the loopback page is http://127.0.0.1, which browsers treat as a secure context, so both real deployments should have the async clipboard API.

WHY: the board reads commit hashes and branch names in tick reports, review comments echoed into #engineering, and the lattice-events channel, and wants to paste them into a terminal without drag-selecting a 7-character token on a phone or a laptop. Selecting short hex runs is fiddly on touch; a one-tap copy removes that.

TENSION WITH THE SAME-DAY "WRITING TO THE BOARD" RULE (#board msg 794; CLAUDE.md section Writing to the board): board-facing messages (DMs to human:forrest, #board, #bizdev) should no longer carry commit hashes or branch names at all -- that evidence moves to the Lattice task. That does NOT make this affordance moot: #engineering, employee-to-employee DMs, and the lattice-events channel (which mirrors board commits verbatim, e.g. "merged 74cb6f9") still carry hashes and branch names by design, and the board reads those channels too. The affordance is worth having; the planner should not re-derive this.

WHERE RENDERING HAPPENS (the seam the planner starts from):
  - apps/chat/public/app.js bodyNode(message) is the single body renderer. It runs tokenizeInline (public/markdown.js: code / strong / em / link, code first, single level) over the whole body, then appendRefLeaf(parent, text, refs, {autolink}) over every plain-text leaf INCLUDING the inner of code/strong/em/link spans. appendRefLeaf is a fixed chain of pure tokenizers in a recorded order: tokenizeUrls (AS-54, terminal -- URL text is never fed further) -> tokenizeAsRefs (AS-10, matches only refs the server resolved) -> tokenizeMsgRefs (AS-26, "msg 156") -> tokenizeFileRefs (AS-26 section 5, public/msg-refs.js FILE_RE, .md paths only) -> createTextNode. A hash/branch pass would be one more link in this chain, and its position matters: it must run after the URL pass (a hex run inside a GitHub commit URL must stay part of the URL) and must not steal "AS-87" out of "feat/AS-87-deploy-heartbeat-and-log" -- so the branch tokenizer probably belongs BEFORE tokenizeAsRefs, and the hash tokenizer after msg-refs so the digits of "msg 810" are never read as hex. Order is an acceptance-criterion-grade decision with named falsifiers per M4.
  - Invariants to preserve: tokenizers emit text and structure, never markup (zero innerHTML anywhere -- every node via el()/textContent/createTextNode); every token text is the exact source slice so concatenation round-trips the input; tokenizers are pure modules importable from node:test (existing tests: test/markdown.test.js, test/msg-refs.test.js). Put the new tokenizer(s) in msg-refs.js or a sibling pure module with the same contract so they are unit-testable without a DOM.
  - Hash false positives are the real design question: words made only of a-f letters (facade, decade, deface -- six letters, but seven-plus cases exist) and any all-digit run of 7+ characters (a pid, 2147483648, a timestamp) match a naive hex regex. The planner decides the rule (require at least one digit AND one a-f letter? minimum length 7? word-boundary and not preceded by # or msg?) and, per M4, names the concrete inputs that must NOT tokenize as a numbered criterion. Grep apps/chat/data/export/ for real bodies to calibrate.

LINK-SITE GUARD OVERLAP (AS-93 / AS-98): AS-93 (merged f15c4ad) added a guard that scans public/ for a fourth site assigning an href from the server-baked .url field, and AS-98 (backlog, critical, Chat set) tightens that guard because its pattern is narrower than its English. This task adds a NEW inline clickable element to the body pipeline. It must NOT be an anchor with an href (there is nothing to navigate to), which keeps it outside the subject of that guard entirely -- and the plan must state that explicitly and prove it: the AS-93/AS-98 scan must remain green after this change for the right reason (no href site added), not because the pattern missed it. If AS-98 lands first, its tightened guard is the one to run; if this lands first, the AS-98 planner must know a new clickable element exists in bodyNode. Linked related_to AS-98.

STYLING: BRANDING.md governs the affordance -- inline code today uses the .body code rule (style.css around line 176); a copyable token wants a cursor/hover/copied state built from existing semantic tokens (--color-accent-bg-subtle, --color-border-interactive, --color-focus-ring, etc.), no raw hex, no new colors. Keyboard: the element should be focusable and copy on Enter/Space, or the plan says why not.

TESTS: the tokenizers get node:test coverage in the existing style (exact token slices, round-trip, named negative inputs). Clipboard behaviour has no test harness in this suite (no DOM); the plan says what is guarded by tests and what is verified by a recorded manual check, and counts them separately. Every counted suite run carries --build (CLAUDE.md corollary).

PRIORITY/ORDER: Chat set (title begins "Chat:"), hence critical per the CLAUDE.md scheduling rule; ordering within the set is by age, so it joins the tail of the age queue behind the remaining chat-app follow-ups (AS-87, AS-88, AS-92, AS-98, AS-102, AS-103, AS-112, AS-113) unless the board says otherwise. Planner: cto-owen or a developer as tech lead; implementer: either developer; reviewer: a qa-* who did not implement.

data.body: Filed on the board's behalf from DM msg 793 (tick watcher:92536 loop tick 3). Priority critical because it is a Chat-set task (CLAUDE.md scheduling rule, DM msg 557), so lattice next reflects Chat-first; ordering WITHIN the set is by age, so AS-115 joins the tail of the age queue behind AS-87 (in progress next), AS-88, AS-92, AS-98, AS-102, AS-103, AS-112, AS-113 unless the board says otherwise. Left in backlog; planning is a later stage. Rendering seam, tokenizer order constraints, the AS-93/AS-98 href-guard overlap (this must be a non-anchor element), the hash false-positive question, and the tension with the same-day plain-language rule are all in the description so the planner does not re-derive them. Linked related_to AS-98.

PLANNED (cto-owen, tick watcher:53418 loop tick 10). Plan: .lattice/plans/task_01M28WQ53NHZFJB9SKGXX7X5BT.md. Key decisions: (1) hash rule is a word-bounded lowercase [0-9a-f]{7,40} with left fence [A-Za-z0-9_/#-] and right fence 'word char or .+word char', plus a composition rule — all-digit runs admitted only at exactly 7, all-alpha admitted except a 3-word stoplist (acceded/defaced/effaced); calibration on 738 live bodies + 593 export bodies found two REAL single-class hashes (1411753 all-digit, efadfac all-alpha) that the 'digit AND letter' rule in the description would have silently missed, so recall wins. (2) Branch rule admits feat/AS-<n>-<slug> only (18/18 corpus occurrences; no other prefix exists); left fence allows '/' and '.' so origin/feat/... and master...feat/... yield the bare branch; the AS-n inside a branch is NOT a separate task link (whole name = one copy target). (3) The leaf chain in app.js appendRefLeaf is extracted into a pure composer tokenizeLeaf in new public/leaf-refs.js (tokenizeAsRefs moves there) so chain order is red-testable per M4: URLs -> branches -> AS-refs -> msg-refs -> file-refs -> hashes -> text; autolink:false now skips URL, branch and hash passes. Six ordering constraints with falsifiers (O1-O5, O2b/O3b); hash-vs-file order is unobservable and stated as documentation. (4) Element: span.copy-ref role=button tabindex=0, Enter/Space, navigator.clipboard.writeText, insecure-context fallback = select-on-click (no execCommand, no false 'copied'), 1200 ms copied state via class. NO href / no anchor / no setAttribute('href') — proven by AC-17 counter (app.js has exactly 9 .href= sites and 0 setAttribute('href') today; whitespace-insensitive regex), mutant M13 must turn it red while the AS-93 guard stays green. (5) Styling from semantic tokens: the chat app has no token layer, so public/tokens.css becomes a verbatim copy of docs/design/tokens/tokens.css with a byte-parity test, linked before style.css, and <html data-theme=light> pinned (tokens.css flips dark on prefers-color-scheme otherwise -> dark chip on white page). AS-98 merge order: AS-98 first if reviewed first (expected); AS-115 rebases before review and QA runs the tightened guard; zero file overlap expected (this task's source-scan tests live in test/copy-refs.test.js, not api.test.js). AS-88: 8 files, all watch/ + watcher tests + READMEs, no public/ overlap — confirmed. Counts: 29 ACs (19 test-guarded, 10 manual-check), 15 anchored mutants with predicted red sets. Baseline on master 7b1f036: host 542/541/1 skipped; compose -p asc-plan-as115 --build Built 542/535/7 skipped/0 fail (torn down). Predicted +19: host 561/560/1, compose 561/554/7 (+8 more if AS-88 merges first). Slug feat/AS-115-copy-refs. Staffing: developer-marcus implements, qa-ruben reviews. Open questions Q1-Q5 closed with defaults at planning. Nothing needs the board.

Staffing (cto-owen, tick watcher:86819 loop tick 11): plan §11 named Marcus because Lena was on AS-88 at planning time. AS-88 merged last tick, so Lena implements AS-115 and Marcus implements AS-98 — the pairing the AS-98 plan §8 itself calls natural. Reviewer stays Ruben. Scratchpad path is therefore scratchpad/agent-developer-lena/AS-115/, not the Marcus path in §11.

Implementation complete on feat/AS-115-copy-refs (worktree .worktrees/AS-115), branched from post-AS-88 master f383ada; HEAD 124440b, tree clean (git diff --exit-code). Commits: efaa5ee (modules, app.js, styling, tokens.css, index.html, server.js, api.test.js guards), d098f56 (T1–T19), 234dc3e (README), 124440b (parity test pins the source digest).

WHAT: public/copy-refs.js (HASH_RE, HEX_WORDS, admitHash, BRANCH_RE, tokenizeHashes, tokenizeBranches — §3 verbatim); public/leaf-refs.js (tokenizeAsRefs moved from app.js, tokenizeLeaf composer urls → branches → asrefs → msgrefs → filerefs → hashes, autolink:false skips url/branch/hash); app.js appendRefLeaf is a switch over tokenizeLeaf, copyRefNode span role=button tabindex=0 title/data-kind, click (isModifiedClick passthrough) + Enter/Space → copyText → clipboard.writeText then flashCopied (COPIED_MS=1200, restart on repeat) or selectNode fallback; style.css .copy-ref rules exactly as §6 (tokens only); public/tokens.css byte copy; index.html links /tokens.css before /style.css and pins data-theme=light; README paragraph.

TWO THINGS THE PLAN DID NOT ANTICIPATE (both recorded, both boring choices): (1) server.js STATIC_FILES is an explicit allowlist — the three new public/ files 404'd until added (copy-refs.js, leaf-refs.js, tokens.css). (2) Four existing api.test.js guards encode the old structure and went red on the extraction: AS-26 (app.js imports msg-refs.js — now via leaf-refs.js, asserted on the served leaf-refs.js), AS-54 (URL-pass order/terminality read from appendRefLeaf control flow — now proven red in leaf-refs.test.js T8/T11; guard retargeted to: leaf-refs.js imports tokenizeUrls from markdown.js, app.js never calls tokenizeUrls itself, autolink:false call site verbatim, appendRefLeaf renders through tokenizeLeaf(text, refs, opts)), AS-74 (served-module count 12 → 14), AS-72 (timer scan found flashCopied's setTimeout — pinned as exactly one setTimeout(…, COPIED_MS) inside flashCopied and excluded from the poll-cadence rules, which still bind the two intervals). So api.test.js IS touched — a seam with AS-98, which §7 predicted as zero; my edits are at the AS-26/54/72/74 tests (lines ~761–830, ~840, ~1050–1075, ~1403), not the AS-93 link-site guard at ~1957–2005, so a rebase should be textually clean. Also (3) T16 in the compose image: the build context is apps/chat, so docs/design/tokens/tokens.css does not exist in the container and the first compose run was 569/561/1 (T16 red). Fix: the test pins the source file's sha256 (a35909d4…df634) and checks the served copy against it always, plus byte parity whenever docs/ is readable — no skip, so compose skips stay 7. The rule for the next editor: edit docs/, copy, update the pin.

COUNTS: host node --test 550/549/0/1 skipped (post-AS-88 baseline) → 569/568/0/1 skipped (+19 as §9 predicts). Compose: docker compose -p asc-impl-as115 run --build --rm test via /usr/local/bin/docker → 'Image asc-impl-as115-test Built', 569 tests / 562 pass / 0 fail / 7 skipped (= §9's post-AS-88 prediction); torn down with down -v --rmi local (Network asc-impl-as115_default Removed).

MUTANTS (15/15 red, 0 survivors; scratch copies via scratchpad/agent-developer-lena/AS-115/mutate.mjs, each anchored to its site with an applied-at-site assertion; full suite per mutant; 'deploy-shape' appears in every scratch run because that test runs git ls-files and the temp copy is not a git repo — an artifact, green in the worktree, excluded below): M1 {7,40}→{8,40}: T1, T3, T7, T10, T13, T14 — WIDER than predicted (T1, T13): every test whose fixture holds a 7-char hash goes red; prediction error, not guard weakness. M2 drop # fence: T2. M3 admitHash→true: T2, T3 (as predicted). M5 slug +→*: T6 only (the predicted asymmetry; T5 stays green). M6 drop / from branch lookahead: T6. M7 remove \.?: T2, T7 (as predicted). M8 url tokens not terminal: T8, T11, T13, T14 (T14 extra — fixture token count). M9a swap branch/asref: T9, T13, T14. M10 hash before msgrefs: T10. M11 autolink gates URL only: T12. M12 one byte flipped in public/tokens.css: T16. M13 node.href='' in copyRefNode: T17 ONLY — the AS-93 link-site guard stayed green, which is the point of AC-17. M14 drop data-theme: T18. M15 hex literal in .copy-ref: T19.

§8b MANUAL CHECKS C1–C10: NOT performed by me — this lane had no browser and the tick's hard time bound; QA performs them cold (the plan already requires that). Q5 (span vs <button>) therefore rests on the reviewer's C5; if selection excludes the span, that is the implementation-level finding §12 pre-authorises and the switch is small.

§12: Q1 16-hex build ids chip (default kept). Q2 no aria-live. Q3 bare branch without origin/ (as built). Q4 tokens app-wide out of scope. Q5 pending C5.

Merge order per §7: AS-98 first if reviewed first; this branch rebases over it before its own review sweep. Reviewer: Ruben (plan §11).

REVIEW (qa-ruben, cold; Opus per the Fable fallback; tick watcher:86819 loop tick 13): PASS on the 19 test-guarded criteria with 0 blocking findings and 0 inline fixes; the 10 manual browser checks (C1-C10) were NOT PERFORMED by either lane and remain unverified — see F1. No implementation-level or plan-level rework needed. Head reviewed: 124440b on feat/AS-115-copy-refs (worktree clean, no rework commits by me). Lena implementation comment read LAST, for counts only.

FINDINGS OUTSIDE THE CRITERIA LIST (5; none blocking):
F1 [completeness finding on this review, not on the code] C1-C10 NOT PERFORMED. I started a scratch server (worktree apps/chat, PORT=8399, scratch CHAT_DB under my scratchpad, never the live 8347/DB) and seeded a fixture message covering C1/C5/C6/C7/C10 shapes, but the c11 browser command is denied to this headless lane, so no browser was available — same gap as Lena reported. 10 of 29 criteria (clipboard write, copied flash, Enter/Space, modified-click, drag-select, code/bold, link-label, no-clipboard fallback, dark-mode pin, whole-branch chip) are therefore unobserved by anyone. What I could verify headlessly: the scratch server serves /copy-refs.js, /leaf-refs.js, /tokens.css (200, correct content-types), index.html carries data-theme=light with /tokens.css linked ahead of /style.css, and the fixture message reads back; copyRefNode is built via el() (textContent) with no href of any spelling. Recommendation for the orchestrator: have a live session with a browser run C1-C10 against a scratch server before or immediately after merge; a failure there is an implementation-level bug to file, not grounds to hold the 19 proven criteria.
F2 [plan-text, convention] Plan §4 O5 example is inconsistent with its own non-goal: tokenizeLeaf("e5a180a on feat/AS-88-x https://x.test", refs, {autolink:false}) with refs containing AS-88 yields text, asref(AS-88), text — not "a single text token" — because AS-refs deliberately still fire inside link labels (§2 non-goal). Observed (my probe L9): autolink:false on "e5a180a feat/AS-115-x https://x.test" -> [text "e5a180a feat/", asref AS-115, text "-x https://x.test"]. Behaviour is as designed; only the example row is wrong. Route to the plan owner (Owen); no code change.
F3 [observation, by design §3.1] Any 7-digit integer chips: "port 8347000", "8100000", and the fraction of "3.1234567" all produce a hash chip. Accepted by the plan (recall over precision, Q1). Recorded so the board knows why a 7-digit number is clickable if it comes up.
F4 [observation, not in corpus] Non-ASCII letters are not fences: "éabc1234" and "abc1234é" both chip. Zero corpus hits; note only.
F5 [observation on my own harness] My first mutant battery reported 11 of 11 mutants surviving including a byte flip in tokens.css — a vacuous pass in my harness (it parsed the spec reporter for TAP "not ok" lines), caught by the cardinality rule (a byte-flip that survives a byte-equality test is impossible). Re-run with --test-reporter=tap; results below are from the corrected run. Recorded because it is exactly the failure mode the review gate exists to catch, and it happened to the reviewer.

ADVERSARIAL PROBES (M6): 32 hash inputs, 14 branch inputs, 14 composer inputs beyond the P/N/BP/BN sets (script scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/AS-115/probe.mjs). All 60 round-trip. Punctuation adjacency (quotes, angle brackets, braces, apostrophe, tab, newline, unicode punctuation) fences correctly; 0x-prefixed hex does not chip; v1234567 does not; 41-char run does not; refs/heads/feat/... and feat/AS-115-copy-refs.md yield the bare branch; double-dash slug does not chip. Composer: msg 1234567 stays a msgref; a hash inside a commit URL stays inside the url token; fileref path segments never chip; task_ ids do not. Performance: 260 KB body with 10,003 tokens in 11 ms; 100 k-char hex run 0 ms; no backtracking cliff. DOM safety: every node built via el()/createTextNode; the AS-74 sink scan now examines 14 public modules (count pinned). SSE/live path: applyMessage renders through the same bodyNode -> appendRefLeaf -> tokenizeLeaf as initial load (one render path, app.js 280-298), so chips are identical on live append. app.js refactor: tokenizeAsRefs moved verbatim (T15 pins), appendRefLeaf is a switch over tokenizeLeaf, the AS-26/54/72/74 api.test.js guards retargeted to leaf-refs.js — the AS-54 terminality guard moved from control-flow reading to observed red (M8), which is stronger than what it replaced.

MUTANTS (scratch copy under my scratchpad, never the task worktree; each asserted applied at the anchored site and restored; harness scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/AS-115/mutants.mjs): 11 run, 11 red, 0 survivors. Exact-match: M3 {T2,T3}, M10 {T10}, M11 {T12}, M13 node.href=empty {T17}, M13b setAttribute(href) {T17}, M14 {T18}, M15 {T19}. Wider in the guard favour: M1 {7,40}->{8,40} red {T1,T3,T7,T10,T13,T14} vs predicted {T1,T13} (every fixture with a 7-char hash); M8 url non-terminal red {T8,T11,T13,T14} vs {T8,T11,T13} (T11 present, so M8 hit the intended site — AC-11 condition met); M9a swap branch/AS-ref red {T9,T13,T14} vs {T9}; M12 tokens.css byte flip red {T16,T19} vs {T16} (T19 also resolves the referenced tokens against tokens.css — a useful property, not a defect). Not run for time: M2, M5, M6, M7 (Lena reports them red; her M1/M8/M9a wider sets match mine exactly).

AS-98 SEAM (plan §7): scratch detached worktree from feat/AS-115-copy-refs, git merge --no-commit feat/AS-98-href-allowlist-guard — auto-merged clean (README.md, api.test.js, + link-sites.test.js). link-sites + api + copy-refs + leaf-refs: 85 tests / 85 pass / 0 fail. Then the chip given node.setAttribute(href) in the seam copy: red exactly twice — T17 (AC-17) and link-sites AS-98 mechanism ban — restored, merge aborted, scratch worktree removed. The chip is green under AS-98 because no href is assigned, proven, not argued. Either merge order is safe.

COUNTS (cardinality before quantification): host node --test in the worktree apps/chat: 569 tests / 568 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped (master baseline 550/549/1; +19 as predicted, 0 new skips). Compose: /usr/local/bin/docker compose -p asc-review-as115 run --build --rm test via node spawnSync — receipt line "Image asc-review-as115-test Built"; 569 / 562 pass / 0 fail / 7 skipped, exit 0; down --rmi local, network removed. Both match Lena reported numbers.

FLOOR CHECK (labelled as such; 5 findings outside the list above, 0 blocking): AC-1..AC-19 — 19 of 19 pass, each by observed green plus the mutant reds above for AC-1/3/8/9/10/11/12/16/17/18/19 (AC-2/5/6/7 by Lena mutants, not re-run). C1-C10: 0 of 10 performed (F1). Q1-Q5: defaults applied; Q5 (span vs button) cannot be settled without C5.

CLEANUP: scratch server pid 15932 killed; scratch worktree removed (git worktree list shows only master, AS-102, AS-115, AS-98); compose project asc-review-as115 torn down; task worktree status clean at 124440b. Untouched: .worktrees/AS-98 and Priya lane. The .lattice dirt in the main checkout for task_01M26C7SHH3G5YDP39FGXQHX6W is not mine and was left alone.

Need: board decision on merging with the ten §8b browser checks unverified. Ruben's review passes all 19 test-guarded criteria (0 blocking findings) at 124440b, but C1-C10 were performed by nobody: Lena had no browser in her lane and the c11 browser is denied to headless QA. PR opened for the board: https://github.com/malls/american-software/pull/2 (review comment posted there). Options put to the board in DM: (a) say 'merge' — Owen merges, the watcher deploys within a minute, the board clicks a hash in the chat app to confirm and any defect becomes a follow-up task; (b) the board runs C1-C10 first against a scratch server from .worktrees/AS-115 (README names the env vars; use a scratch data dir and a port other than 8347). The next tick merges on the board's word. Ruben's F2 (plan §4 O5 example row contradicts the non-goal) is a plan-text correction I will append at merge; F3/F4 (7-digit integers chip; non-ASCII letters are not hash fences) are recorded as by-design, no corpus hits.
